evidence.excerpt: Parent-teacher meeting ran late. Most parents didn't show up, same as last month. Spent the rest of the evening marking notebooks and helping Amma sort the kitchen.

Went to the literacy camp in Sultanpur today and I keep thinking about this one girl, maybe seven or eight, who was holding the pencil like she'd never held one before. And honestly she probably hadn't. She was gripping it...

coach_narrative.weekly_mirror: The parent-teacher meeting ran late, and you still spent the evening “marking notebooks and helping Amma sort the kitchen.” At the literacy camp in Sultanpur, the girl holding a pencil for perhaps the first time stayed with you, connecting your everyday responsibilities with your care for making the world a fairer, better place.
coach_narrative.tension_explanation: You were carrying several kinds of responsibility: noticing that many parents did not attend, helping at home, and being present with a child beginning to learn. The meaning of that encounter seems to have stayed open and vivid for you.
coach_narrative.reflective_question: When you think of the girl in Sultanpur now, what part of that moment remains with you most?
